- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is trending up, reduce overshoot by 10–15% in the next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) after a spike, model should not overcorrect; instead, allow a 5–10% downward lag to match true mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if recent 5-day average is rising, model should not overpredict 30-day peak; cap forecast at 1.5x recent 5-day high.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model should not assume strong trend; use 20-day moving average as baseline for correction.  
- When true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model should not predict further drop; instead, adjust downward only if sentiment confirms bearish shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3 days show strong downward momentum, model should not forecast upward unless sentiment > 0.8.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, model should not ignore sentiment and should adjust forecast downward by 5–10% to match sentiment bias.  
- If model overpredicts 30-day peak by >10% and sentiment is neutral, reduce forecast by 5–8% to align with mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model should not overreact; reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid false bullish signal.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly down, model should not overreact; forecast should be capped at 1.2x recent 5-day average.
